body: Me and my wife went to this place a few months back, and it was a place that we could actually spend hours without being bored.Being tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka, it is located in a very calm, quiet and a very nice area without being urbanized. The environment and the climate is very comforting, the air and the water in the area is so clean and it truly is a place for relaxation. You can get into the water where the water falls, but this place seemed to be less dangerous as well (but not sure, so be careful). The road to the waterfall is rough, but I saw even small cars had arrived. However, that definitely would be a worthy trip ultimately! It is not a very crowded place, so you can stay for a long without rushing! You will have to buy a ticket, but it's cheap. If you want to buy some food, please keep it purchased earlier because you wouldn't find many stalls out there. Anyway, please do not throw any empty food containers or garbage in this area; because, it's a place that everybody should try to protect for the future!!!

body: Bambarakanda Waterfall is the longest water fall in Sri Lanka. The journey to the bottom of the fall is through a narrow and difficult climb.It is a motorable road but at the top you have to walk a few meters to reach the water fall. The view of the fall is fantastic but recommend only for those appreciating scenic beauty. From Colombo you go through Ratnapura and take the Balangoda road. Balangoda has a beautiful Rest House where you can have a good Rice and Curry meal. From Balangoda you drive up to Haputale through Beragala. From Beragala you can see all the way to Uda Walawe and Kirinda in deep south on a clear day. The road to Bambarakanda is between Beragala and Haputale. If you want to see Bambarakanda falls I suggest you stay over at Haputale for the night. There are enough vacation rentals and a new hotel to stay in Haputale. From Haputale you can go down to Bandarawela another Holiday town. While in Haputale you should visit Adisham Bungalow a former residence of a scottish gentlemen now run by the catholic priests.The scenic drive from Balangoda to Bandarawela is worth doing when holidaying in Sri Lanka. My last visit was around August 2012.I rate the Bambarakanda Waterfall visit average because of the roadway leading to falls but the waterfall is worth seing.

body: After passing Beluhuloya on A4 road close to Kalupahana you will come across weli oya bridge . Just passing weli oya bridge you get a narrow road on to your left. At the starting point of that gap you will see small shops and a small bo-tree with a buddha statue. The road is a narrow one but tarred and quite ok. You have to travel about 3km on this road and there is a place to park the vehicles . To reach the bottom of the fall you have to walk on a small track through pine forest. At the bottom of the fall , there's a lovely pool and you must take a bath . The water is very cold and it will refresh you the moment you get in to water. When we went there, there were no rains and it is dry season and there were very little water. Village folks said November - February they get a lot of rains and after that the fall starts to have the full flow. We saw a lot of construction work is carrying out and it will ease the visitors to reach the water fall but it is taking off the natural beauty of the surrounding. visited September 2013

title: No words to explain the beauty
body: Bambarakanda is the tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka; situated in Kalupahana in Badulla district.There are two ways to reach Bambarakanda; both are full of unbelievable sceneries:Colombo-->Ratnapura-->Balangoda-->KalupahanaBadulla-->Bandarawella-->Haputale-->Beragala-->KalupahanaWe stayed at Sera Mayakaduwa’s lodge; who is well-known as the lonely lady who takes the care of Bambarakanda fall.The rock which is next to the waterfall looks like a couple hugging each others (knows as the Bambarakanda Lovers). Best view of this can be seen at the Sera’s lodge. Before the Bambarakanda we went to the Lanka Ella which is another amazing waterfall, situated very close to Bambarakanda. There are 2 ways to reach Lanka Ella. Harder one is with rock climbing which needs bit of experience in hiking. Easy one through a lovely Pine forest. On our way, we went to the Bambarakanda base and had a nice shower from the base pool. Its a priceless experience. No words to explain the beauty of the sceneries.
